claim: A consanguineous Pakistani family with infertile males was recruited for the study.
source: A consanguineous Pakistani family with infertile males was recruited (Figure 1A).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript text describing the study subjects.

claim: Both infertile males (IV-1 and IV-2) have failed to have child over 3 years of unprotected sex after marriage.
source: Both infertile males (IV-1 and IV-2) have failed to have child over 3 years of unprotected sex after marriage (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Clinical data from patient records documented in supplementary materials.

claim: The male infertile patients do not show PCD-related symptoms, abnormal heights, weights, secondary characteristics, nor anatomical defects.
source: The male infertile patients do not show PCD-related symptoms, abnormal heights, weights, secondary characteristics, nor anatomical defects.
evidence: Clinical examination data of the patients.

claim: The infertile patients have normal karyotypes without Y chromosome microdeletion.
source: They also have normal karyotypes without Y chromosome microdeletion.
evidence: Genetic testing results from patient samples.

claim: The spermatozoa from the infertile patients showed an overall normal morphology.
source: Overall, the Papanicolaou (PAP) stained spermatozoa from the infertile patients showed an overall normal morphology (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Microscopic analysis of stained sperm samples shown in figures.

claim: The infertile patients have normal ranges of abnormal sperm morphology assessed by clinical semen analysis.
source: which was further supported by normal ranges of abnormal sperm morphology assessed by clinical semen analysis (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Clinical semen analysis data documented in supplementary materials.

claim: The progressive motility of sperm from infertile patients was lower than the World Health Organization (WHO) standard.
source: However, their progressive motility was lower than the World Health Organization (WHO) standard (World Health Organization, 2010)
evidence: Clinical semen analysis compared to WHO reference values.

claim: The patients were clinically diagnosed as asthenozoospermia (ASZ).
source: and the patients were clinically diagnosed as ASZ (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Clinical diagnosis based on semen analysis results.

claim: Whole exome sequencing estimated 5.02% inbreeding co-efficiency in the proband.
source: WES estimated 5.02% inbreeding co-efficiency and the longest homozygous-by-descent segment as 37.5 cM, verifying the consanguineous nature of the recruited family.

claim: The longest homozygous-by-descent segment in the proband was 37.5 cM.
source: WES estimated 5.02% inbreeding co-efficiency and the longest homozygous-by-descent segment as 37.5 cM, verifying the consanguineous nature of the recruited family.

claim: A homozygous splicing donor site variant (c.621+1 G>A) in LRRC23 was identified.
source: Among the four identified rare variants (Supplementary file 2), only one homozygous splicing donor site variant (c.621+1 G>A) in LRRC23 (leucin-rich repeat containing protein 23) is co-segregated with the male infertility phenotype (Figure 1A, C and D).
evidence: WES data analysis and validation by Sanger sequencing.

claim: The LRRC23 variant co-segregates with the male infertility phenotype in the family.
source: Among the four identified rare variants (Supplementary file 2), only one homozygous splicing donor site variant (c.621+1 G>A) in LRRC23 (leucin-rich repeat containing protein 23) is co-segregated with the male infertility phenotype (Figure 1A, C and D).
evidence: Genetic analysis showing variant segregation pattern matches phenotype in family members.

claim: The variant at the splicing donor site of LRRC23 intron 5 is predicted to prevent splicing out of the intron.
source: The variant at the splicing donor site of LRRC23 intron 5 is predicted to prevent splicing out of the intron, which can lead to early termination of protein translation with loss of 136 amino acids at the C-terminus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).

claim: The variant can lead to early termination of protein translation with loss of 136 amino acids at the C-terminus.
source: The variant at the splicing donor site of LRRC23 intron 5 is predicted to prevent splicing out of the intron, which can lead to early termination of protein translation with loss of 136 amino acids at the C-terminus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: Computational prediction based on sequence analysis.

claim: 293T cells transfected with the construct carrying the variant failed to splice out the intronic region.
source: 293T cells transfected with the construct carrying the variant failed to splice out the intronic region (Figure 1F)
evidence: RT-PCR analysis of transfected cells shown in Figure 1F.

claim: 293T cells transfected with the variant construct generated only truncated LRRC23.
source: and generated only truncated LRRC23 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).

claim: The variant is pathogenic and explains the male infertility with defective sperm motility in this family.
source: These results suggest the variant is pathogenic and explains the male infertility with defective sperm motility in this family.
evidence: Inference based on functional validation experiments and co-segregation analysis.

claim: LRRC23 is a radial spoke (RS) component.
source: LRRC23 is a radial spoke (RS) component (Padma et al., 2003).

claim: Genetic ablation of Lrrc23 in mice causes severe sperm motility defects and male infertility.
source: Consistent with the ASZ phenotype in our infertile patients with a new splice mutation in LRRC23, genetic ablation of Lrrc23 in mice causes severe sperm motility defects and male infertility (Zhang et al., 2021).

claim: Lrrc23 mutant mice were generated by CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing to mimic the predicted outcome in human patients.
source: To better understand detailed function of LRRC23 and the molecular pathogenicity of the identified variant, we generated Lrrc23 mutant mice by CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing to mimic the predicted outcome in human patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Description of experimental methods and results.

claim: Two mouse lines with 4126 or 4135 bp deletion (Lrrc23-4126del and Lrrc23-4135del) were established.
source: We established two mouse lines with 4126 or 4135 bp deletion (Lrrc23-4126del and Lrrc23-4135del, respectively; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Genotyping results of generated mouse lines.

claim: Both homozygous Lrrc23-4126del and 4135del mice displayed identical male infertility and defective sperm motility phenotypes.
source: Both homozygous Lrrc23-4126del and 4135del mice displayed the identical male infertility and defective sperm motility phenotypes in our initial characterization.
evidence: Phenotypic characterization of both mouse lines.

claim: Truncated Lrrc23 mRNA is expressed from the mutant Lrrc23 allele.
source: We observed that truncated Lrrc23 mRNA is expressed from the mutant Lrrc23 allele but the total mRNA level of Lrrc23 in testis is not different from wildtype (WT) to that in Lrrc23Δ/Δ males (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–F).

claim: The total mRNA level of Lrrc23 in testis is not different between WT and Lrrc23Δ/Δ males.
source: We observed that truncated Lrrc23 mRNA is expressed from the mutant Lrrc23 allele but the total mRNA level of Lrrc23 in testis is not different from wildtype (WT) to that in Lrrc23Δ/Δ males (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–F).

claim: The truncated Lrrc23 mRNA would produce mutant LRRC23 containing 27 non-native amino acids translated from 3' UTR instead of 136 amino acids at the C-terminus.
source: Sequencing the truncated Lrrc23 mRNA revealed that the transcript would produce mutant LRRC23 containing 27 non-native amino acids translated from 3' UTR instead of 136 amino acids at the C-terminus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).

claim: The truncated LRRC23 is detected only marginally in the microsome fraction of Lrrc23Δ/Δ testis.
source: Despite the comparable Lrrc23 mRNA levels in WT and Lrrc23Δ/Δ testis, the truncated LRRC23 is detected only marginally in the microsome fraction of Lrrc23Δ/Δ testis, different from full-length LRRC23 enriched in the cytosolic fraction of WT testis (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).

claim: Full-length LRRC23 is enriched in the cytosolic fraction of WT testis.
source: Despite the comparable Lrrc23 mRNA levels in WT and Lrrc23Δ/Δ testis, the truncated LRRC23 is detected only marginally in the microsome fraction of Lrrc23Δ/Δ testis, different from full-length LRRC23 enriched in the cytosolic fraction of WT testis (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).

claim: The mutant LRRC23 is not present in epididymal sperm.
source: In addition, the mutant LRRC23 is not present in epididymal sperm (Figure 2B and C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C–E)
evidence: Immunoblot and immunofluorescence analysis of sperm.

claim: The C-terminal region is essential for proper LRRC23 transportation to the sperm flagella.
source: indicating that the C-terminal region is essential for proper LRRC23 transportation to the sperm flagella.
evidence: Inference from the absence of mutant LRRC23 in sperm despite its presence in testis.

claim: Sperm from Lrrc23Δ/Δ and Lrrc23-4135delΔ/Δ males are morphologically normal.
source: Sperm from Lrrc23Δ/Δ and Lrrc23-4135delΔ/Δ males are morphologically normal (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E and F)

claim: The epididymal sperm counts of Lrrc23+/Δ and Lrrc23Δ/Δ males are not significantly different.
source: and the epididymal sperm counts of Lrrc23+/Δ and Lrrc23Δ/Δ males are not significantly different (Figure 2D).

claim: Lrrc23Δ/Δ males are 100% infertile.
source: Despite the normal morphology and sperm counts, Lrrc23Δ/Δ males are 100% infertile (Figure 2E and F).

claim: Lrrc23Δ/Δ females are fertile.
source: By contrast, Lrrc23Δ/Δ females are fertile, which supports the IV-4's infertility is not likely due to the identified variant (Figure 1A).
evidence: Mating test results with mutant females.

claim: Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm motility parameters are significantly altered compared to Lrrc23+/Δ sperm.
source: Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm motility parameters are significantly altered compared to Lrrc23+/Δ sperm (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).

claim: Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm cannot swim efficiently under viscous conditions that mimic the environment in female reproductive tract.
source: Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm cannot swim efficiently under viscous conditions that mimic the environment in female reproductive tract (Figure 2G and Video 1)
evidence: Swimming trajectory analysis in viscous media.

claim: Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm flagella just vibrate but do not beat normally.
source: and their flagella just vibrate but do not beat normally (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 2H and Video 2).

claim: Inducing capacitation did not rescue any observed motility defect of Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: In addition, inducing capacitation did not rescue any observed motility defect of Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm as demonstrated by flagellar waveform analysis, and CASA measurement of curvilinear velocity (VCL), straight line velocity (VSL), and amplitude of lateral head (ALH).
evidence: Motility analysis before and after capacitation.

claim: The C-terminal truncation dysregulates the flagellar localization of the mutant LRRC23, leading to sperm motility defects and male infertility.
source: These results suggest the C-terminal truncation dysregulates the flagellar localization of the mutant LRRC23, leading to sperm motility defects and male infertility.
evidence: Inference from combined localization and motility data.

claim: T-shaped RS structures (i.e., head and stalk) are conserved across species.
source: Recent cryo-ET studies revealed that T-shaped RS structures (i.e., head and stalk) are conserved across the species (Leung et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2014; Figure 3A).
evidence: Cited from cryo-ET studies and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Three RSs (RS1, RS2, and RS3) are repeated in a 96 nm interval along the flagellar axoneme in mammalian sperm, sea urchin sperm, Trypanosoma brucei, and Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
source: Three RSs (RS1, RS2, and RS3) are repeated in a 96 nm interval along the flagellar axoneme in mammalian sperm, sea urchin sperm, Trypanosoma brucei, and even in C. reinhardtii with stump-like RS3 without a head structure (Figure 3A).

claim: LRRC23 is a RS protein in chordate axoneme.
source: LRRC23 is a RS protein in chordate axoneme and has been considered especially as the orthologue of RSP15, a RS2 stalk protein in C. reinhardtii (Han et al., 2018; Satouh and Inaba, 2009; Yang et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2021; Figure 3B).

claim: LRRC23 has been considered as the orthologue of RSP15, a RS2 stalk protein in C. reinhardtii.
source: LRRC23 is a RS protein in chordate axoneme and has been considered especially as the orthologue of RSP15, a RS2 stalk protein in C. reinhardtii (Han et al., 2018; Satouh and Inaba, 2009; Yang et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2021; Figure 3B).

claim: hLRRC23WT interacts only with RSPH9, a RS head protein, among the head and stalk RSPH proteins tested.
source: This trap assay demonstrated that hLRRC23WT interacts only with RSPH9, a RS head protein, among the head and stalk RSPH proteins tested (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: RSPH-trap assay results shown in figures.

claim: hLRRC23Mut does not interact with RSPH9.
source: Markedly, hLRRC23Mut does not interact with RSPH9, indicating LRRC23 interaction with RS head via its C-terminus.

claim: LRRC23 interacts with RS head via its C-terminus.
source: Markedly, hLRRC23Mut does not interact with RSPH9, indicating LRRC23 interaction with RS head via its C-terminus.
evidence: Inference from the loss of interaction in C-terminal truncation mutant.

claim: C. reinhardtii RSP15 has the highest sequence homology to LRRC34, not LRRC23, in Ciona intestinalis.
source: To test this new hypothesis, we performed BLAST search and found C. reinhardtii RSP15 (Gui et al., 2021) has the highest sequence homology to LRRC34, not LRRC23, in Ciona intestinalis.

claim: LRRC34 orthologs are evolutionarily closer to RSP15 orthologs than LRRC23 orthologs.
source: Our phylogenetic and pairwise distance comparison analyses also revealed that LRRC34 orthologs are evolutionarily closer to RSP15 orthologs than LRRC23 orthologs (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).

claim: AlphaFold-predicted structure of human LRRC34, but not that of LRRC23, presents the same structural features as those of RSP15.
source: Moreover, AlphaFold-predicted structure of human LRRC34, but not that of LRRC23, presents the same structural features as those of RSP15 (i.e. repeated leucin-rich repeat domains and an α-helix motif in-between) (Figure 3H).

claim: LRRC34 and LRRC23 share their gene expression patterns among tissues, most abundantly expressed in the tissues known for ciliary and flagellar function such as retina, testis, and fallopian tube.
source: LRRC34 and LRRC23 share their gene expression patterns among tissues, most abundantly expressed in the tissues known for ciliary and flagellar function such as retina, testis, and fallopian tube (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: Gene expression data from tissue databases.

claim: LRRC34 is a ciliary and flagellar protein and likely the RSP15 orthologue in chordates.
source: All these results suggest that LRRC34 is a ciliary and flagellar protein and likely the RSP15 orthologue in chordates, and that LRRC23 function is associated with the RS head.
evidence: Inference from sequence, structural, and expression analyses.

claim: LRRC23 function is associated with the RS head.
source: All these results suggest that LRRC34 is a ciliary and flagellar protein and likely the RSP15 orthologue in chordates, and that LRRC23 function is associated with the RS head.
evidence: Inference from interaction studies and structural analyses.

claim: Confocal imaging of immunostained sperm did not show any difference on the subflagellar localization of axonemal or peri-axonemal proteins between Lrrc23+/Δ and Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: Confocal imaging of immunostained sperm by antibodies against various proteins of known localization did not show any difference on the subflagellar localization of axonemal or peri-axonemal proteins (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The levels of flagellar proteins are not significantly different between Lrrc23+/Δ and Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: The levels of such flagellar proteins are also not significantly different between Lrrc23+/Δ and in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).

claim: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) did not reveal apparent structural abnormalities in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm flagella.
source: Furthermore, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) did not reveal apparent structural abnormalities in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm flagella (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Overall subflagellar and ultrastructural organization in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm is preserved despite almost complete loss of sperm motility.
source: These results indicate overall subflagellar and ultrastructural organization in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm is preserved despite almost complete loss of sperm motility.
evidence: Inference from microscopy and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Any structural abnormality in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm would be subtle and local in the axoneme, likely in the RS head region.
source: Any structural abnormality in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm would be subtle and local in the axoneme, likely in the RS head region, which requires a higher resolution microscope technique.
evidence: Inference from the absence of gross structural defects but presence of motility defects.

claim: In WT sperm, the three RSs are repeated with a typical pattern, in which RS1 and RS2 are recognized by an additional EM density between them (barrel structure) followed by RS3.
source: In WT sperm, the three RSs are repeated with a typical pattern, in which RS1 and RS2 are recognized by an additional EM density between them (barrel structure, Leung et al., 2021) followed by RS3 (Figure 4C, left).

claim: In Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm, EM densities corresponding to RS3 are significantly weaker than those in WT sperm.
source: In Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm, EM densities corresponding to RS3 are significantly weaker than those in WT sperm, whereas the structural features of RS1 and RS2 are overall kept unaltered from that of WT sperm (Figure 4C, right).

claim: The structural features of RS1 and RS2 are overall kept unaltered in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm compared to WT sperm.
source: In Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm, EM densities corresponding to RS3 are significantly weaker than those in WT sperm, whereas the structural features of RS1 and RS2 are overall kept unaltered from that of WT sperm (Figure 4C, right).

claim: The LRRC23 mutation specifically disorganizes RS3 in the sperm axoneme.
source: These results strongly indicate that the LRRC23 mutation specifically disorganizes RS3 in the sperm axoneme.

claim: The head region of RS3 is entirely missing in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: Remarkably, the resulting 3D maps reveal that the head region of RS3 is entirely missing in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm, whereas the heads of RS1 and RS2 are intact (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Sub-tomogram averaging analysis of cryo-ET data.

claim: The heads of RS1 and RS2 are intact in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: Remarkably, the resulting 3D maps reveal that the head region of RS3 is entirely missing in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm, whereas the heads of RS1 and RS2 are intact (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Sub-tomogram averaging analysis of cryo-ET data.

claim: The junctional structure between RS2 and RS3 is specifically abolished in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: In addition, superimposition of the 3D STA maps demonstrates that the junctional structure between RS2 and RS3–present in mouse and human sperm but not in C. reinhardtii nor in T. brucei flagellar axoneme–is also specifically abolished in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm (Figure 5C).
evidence: Superimposition analysis of sub-tomogram averaging maps.

claim: The junctional structure between RS2 and RS3 is present in mouse and human sperm but not in C. reinhardtii nor in T. brucei flagellar axoneme.
source: In addition, superimposition of the 3D STA maps demonstrates that the junctional structure between RS2 and RS3–present in mouse and human sperm but not in C. reinhardtii nor in T. brucei flagellar axoneme–is also specifically abolished in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm (Figure 5C).

claim: Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm have intact stalk structures of RS3 like those in WT sperm.
source: By contrast, Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm have intact stalk structures of RS3 like those in WT sperm.

claim: LRRC23 is a RS3 head component.
source: Consistent with the protein-protein interaction between LRRC23 and the RS head protein RSPH9 using the RSPH-trap approach (Figure 3), these direct structural observations unarguably clarify that LRRC23 is a RS3 head component and the absence of the RS3 head leads to motility defects in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
evidence: Inference from combined biochemical and structural data.

claim: The absence of the RS3 head leads to motility defects in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: Consistent with the protein-protein interaction between LRRC23 and the RS head protein RSPH9 using the RSPH-trap approach (Figure 3), these direct structural observations unarguably clarify that LRRC23 is a RS3 head component and the absence of the RS3 head leads to motility defects in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
evidence: Inference from structural and motility analyses.

claim: The C-terminal truncation of LRRC23 prevents the assembly of RS3 head during spermatogenesis.
source: These results demonstrate that the C-terminal truncation of LRRC23 prevents the assembly of RS3 head during spermatogenesis, thus preventing functional RS3 complex formation.
evidence: Inference from structural and localization data.

claim: The C-terminal truncation of LRRC23 prevents functional RS3 complex formation.
source: These results demonstrate that the C-terminal truncation of LRRC23 prevents the assembly of RS3 head during spermatogenesis, thus preventing functional RS3 complex formation.

claim: The morphology of RS3 head is distinguished from those of RS1 and 2 in mouse motile cilia.
source: For example, the morphology of RS3 head is distinguished from those of RS1 and 2 in mouse motile cilia (Zheng et al., 2021).

claim: In the tracheal cilia of PCD patients, RSPH1 or RSPH4 loss-of-function mutation specifically abolished RS1 and RS2 heads, but not RS3 head.
source: Moreover, in the tracheal cilia of the PCD patients, RSPH1 or RSPH4 loss-of-function mutation specifically abolished RS1 and RS2 heads, but not RS3 head (Lin et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2021)

claim: RS3 shares T-shaped structure just like RS1 and RS2 in most eukaryotic motile cilia and flagella.
source: even though RS3 shares T-shaped structure just like RS1 and RS2 in most eukaryotic motile cilia and flagella (Imhof et al., 2019; Leung et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2012; Lin et al., 2014).

claim: LRRC23 is a conserved RS protein in C. intestinalis and mouse.
source: Previous immuno-EM studies showed that LRRC23 is a conserved RS protein in C. intestinalis and mouse (Pigino et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2021).

claim: LRRC23 was originally predicted to be the orthologue of RSP15 in C. reinharditti due to the presence of leucine-rich repeat domains.
source: It is of note that LRRC23 was originally predicted to be the orthologue of RSP15 in C. reinharditti, a RS2 stalk protein, due to the presence of leucine-rich repeat domains (Gui et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2006).

claim: LRRC23 orthologues are not conserved in C. reinharditti in which RS3 is headless and short stump-like.
source: Yet, we found LRRC23 orthologues are not conserved in C. reinharditti in which RS3 is headless and short stump-like, but present in the species where RS3 head structure is preserved, such as T. thermophila, sea urchin, and mammals.

claim: LRRC23 orthologues are present in the species where RS3 head structure is preserved, such as T. thermophila, sea urchin, and mammals.
source: Yet, we found LRRC23 orthologues are not conserved in C. reinharditti in which RS3 is headless and short stump-like, but present in the species where RS3 head structure is preserved, such as T. thermophila, sea urchin, and mammals.

claim: LRRC34 is likely the RSP15 orthologue in chordate animals.
source: Instead of LRRC23, our phylogenetic and structural comparison strongly suggests that LRRC34 is likely the RSP15 orthologue in chordate animals (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1)

claim: LRRC34 is a previously unappreciated component of RS2 stalk.
source: Instead of LRRC23, our phylogenetic and structural comparison strongly suggests that LRRC34 is likely the RSP15 orthologue in chordate animals (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and a previously unappreciated component of RS2 stalk.
evidence: Inference from phylogenetic and structural analyses.

claim: A LRRC34 loss-of-function mutation was identified from ciliopathic children.
source: Identifying a LRRC34 loss-of-function mutation from ciliopathic children further supports that LRRC34 is a RS component (Shamseldin et al., 2020).

claim: LRRC23 is required for assembling the RS3 head structure.
source: Our wild-type-mutant comparison approach using cryo-ET analyses ultimately clarify that LRRC23 is required for assembling the RS3 head structure (Figures 4 and 5), indicating LRRC23 as an RS3 head component.

claim: RSPH9 interacts with LRRC23.
source: Interestingly, a RS head component, RSPH9, interacts with LRRC23 but the protein level or the localization of RSPH9 is not altered in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Biochemical interaction assay and immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: The protein level or the localization of RSPH9 is not altered in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm.
source: Interestingly, a RS head component, RSPH9, interacts with LRRC23 but the protein level or the localization of RSPH9 is not altered in Lrrc23Δ/Δ sperm (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)

claim: RSPH9 could be a head component of RS1 and RS2 like in C. reinhardtii, but not of RS3.
source: suggesting that RSPH9 could be a head component of RS1 and RS2 like in C. reinhardtii (Gui et al., 2021), but not of RS3.
evidence: Inference from interaction data and comparison with C. reinhardtii.

claim: An independent study reported that LRRC23 is required for flagellar localization of the RS stalk and fibrous sheath components in mature sperm.
source: Of note is that an independent study reported that LRRC23 is required for flagellar localization of the RS stalk and fibrous sheath components in mature sperm (Zhang et al., 2021).

claim: The discrepancy between two studies is likely due to the presence of the truncated LRRC23 in testis in Lrrc23Δ/Δ males, which might partly allow flagellar localization of other flagellar components during germ cell development.
source: This discrepancy between two studies is likely due to the presence of the truncated LRRC23 in testis in Lrrc23Δ/Δ males, which might partly allow flagellar localization of other flagellar components during germ cell development.
evidence: Speculation based on observed truncated protein in testis.

claim: LRRC23 is present in tracheal cilia.
source: This conclusion is further supported by the presence of LRRC23 in tracheal cilia (Zhang et al., 2021) that lack the RS2-RS3 bridge structure (Leung et al., 2021).

claim: Tracheal cilia lack the RS2-RS3 bridge structure.
source: This conclusion is further supported by the presence of LRRC23 in tracheal cilia (Zhang et al., 2021) that lack the RS2-RS3 bridge structure (Leung et al., 2021).

claim: A set of three RSs is repeated along the axoneme in motile cilia and flagella.
source: In motile cilia and flagella, a set of three RSs is repeated along the axoneme (Leung et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2012; Lin et al., 2014; Viswanadha et al., 2017).

claim: A recent cryo-ET study revealed additional RS substructures in mammalian sperm flagella, a barrel structure at RS1 and a junctional bridge structure between RS2 and RS3.
source: Notably, a recent cryo-ET study revealed additional RS substructures in mammalian sperm flagella, a barrel structure at RS1 and a junctional bridge structure between RS2 and RS3 (Leung et al., 2021)

claim: The RS1 barrel and RS2-RS3 bridge structures were not observed in the sea urchin sperm or human motile cilia.
source: which were not observed in the sea urchin sperm or human motile cilia (Lin et al., 2014).

claim: The RS1 barrel and RS2-RS3 bridge structures are asymmetrically distributed along the mammalian sperm axoneme, corresponding to the peripheral MTDs in a species-specific manner.
source: Furthermore, they are asymmetrically distributed along the mammalian sperm axoneme, corresponding to the peripheral MTDs in a species-specific manner (Chen et al., 2023).

claim: Cryo-ET and STA analyses visualized the mammalian sperm-specific RS1 barrel and RS2-RS3 bridge structures in WT sperm flagella.
source: Our cryo-ET and STA analyses visualized the mammalian sperm-specific RS1 barrel and RS2-RS3 bridge structures in WT sperm flagella, consistent with Leung et al., 2021.

claim: In Lrrc23 mutant sperm, most of the EM density corresponding to the RS2-RS3 bridge structure is missing and/or altered together with that of the RS3 head.
source: Strikingly, in Lrrc23 mutant sperm, most of the EM density corresponding to the RS2-RS3 bridge structure is missing and/or altered together with that of the RS3 head (Figures 4 and 5).

claim: The RS2-RS3 bridge structure is absent in tracheal cilia.
source: Considering the absence of RS2-RS3 bridge in tracheal cilia (Lin et al., 2014), LRRC23 also contributes to assemble this flagellar RS substructure.

claim: LRRC23 contributes to assemble the RS2-RS3 bridge structure.
source: Considering the absence of RS2-RS3 bridge in tracheal cilia (Lin et al., 2014), LRRC23 also contributes to assemble this flagellar RS substructure.
evidence: Inference from structural analysis and comparison with tracheal cilia.

claim: The RS3 and RS2-RS3 bridge structures and their sub-axonemal localization confer non-planar and asymmetric flagellar motility unique to mammalian sperm hyperactivation.
source: Thus, we speculate that the RS3 and RS2-RS3 bridge structures and their sub-axonemal localization confer non-planar and asymmetric flagellar motility unique to mammalian sperm hyperactivation.

claim: LRRC23 is required for assembling the RS2-RS3 bridge structure specifically in mammalian sperm flagella.
source: As the RS2-RS3 bridge structure is absent in tracheal cilia (Lin et al., 2014), our study unambiguously demonstrates that LRRC23 is required for assembling this bridge structure specifically in mammalian sperm flagella.
evidence: Inference from structural comparison between sperm and cilia.

claim: LRRC23 may be localized at the junction between RS2-RS3 bridge structure and RS3 head.
source: If so, LRRC23 may be localized at the junction between RS2-RS3 bridge structure and RS3 head.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in various RS components that are common to motile cilia and sperm flagella were reported to cause PCD and/or male infertility.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in various RS components that are common to motile cilia and sperm flagella were reported to cause PCD and/or male infertility.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations of RSPH1 were identified from PCD patients.
source: Loss-of-function mutations of RSPH1 (Knowles et al., 2014; Kott et al., 2013), RSPH3 (Jeanson et al., 2015), RSPH4A and RSPH9 (Castleman et al., 2009) were identified from PCD patients.
